intro: Hi! You can already say what you did with -ed verbs: I walked, I watched. But the most common verbs have their own past form: go → went, eat → ate, buy → bought. In this lesson you learn the top ten, and how to say what you didn't do and ask Did you…? Warm-up: what did you eat yesterday? Try 'I ate …'.
teachingNotes: Indonesian verbs never change for time: only the time word shows the past (Kemarin saya pergi ke pasar). So the #1 error is *'Yesterday I go to the market'. Whenever the learner uses yesterday, last night, last week or ... ago, check that the verb is in the past: went, not go.

Irregular verbs have no rule: present them as words to memorise, in small groups, and recycle them. The core list for this lesson: go → went, have → had, get → got, see → saw, eat → ate, buy → bought, make → made, come → came, take → took, say → said (plus do → did and drink → drank). Two common errors: adding -ed anyway (*goed, *eated, *buyed, *taked) and adding -s for he/she (*she wents). The past form is the same for every person. Pronunciation: said = 'sed', bought = 'bot' (gh silent).

Negatives and questions use did + the base verb (the dictionary form: go, see, eat): I didn't go, Did you see…? Stress the why: did already shows the past, so the main verb goes back to its base form. *'I didn't went' and *'Did you saw…?' show the past twice. Link it to the simple present the learner knows: doesn't takes the -s, so it's 'she doesn't work', not *'doesn't works'. The same goes for regular verbs: *'didn't watched' is wrong.

Questions: Did + subject + base verb (Did Rina buy the tickets?). Short answers use did: Yes, she did. / No, I didn't (rather than just 'Yes, I went'). Wh-questions: question word + did + subject + base verb (Where did they go? What did you eat?). Indonesian asks with statement order and intonation (Kamu pergi ke mana?), so watch for *'Where you went?' and *'You went to Bali?'. Also watch for mixing be and did: *'Were you go…?' and *'I didn't was…'. Sentences with was/were (from the past of be lesson) never use did.

do is both the helper and a real verb: What did you do yesterday? (did = helper, do = melakukan) — I did my homework. Treat 'What did you do at the weekend?' as a key phrase. 'at the weekend' is British; Americans say 'on the weekend'. Both are fine.

Limits: no present perfect (Indonesian 'sudah makan' often needs it; if the learner asks, say it's a later lesson and that with a finished time like yesterday or last week English uses the past simple). Don't teach past participles (gone, seen, eaten), the past continuous, could, will or going to. Keep to the core list above; if the learner meets another irregular verb, just give its past form as a word to remember.

keyPoints.title: Common irregular past forms
keyPoints.explanation: Most verbs add -ed (walked), but many common verbs have their own past form, with no rule: go → went, have → had, get → got, see → saw, eat → ate, buy → bought, make → made, come → came, take → took, say → said. Learn them as words. Don't add -ed (not 'goed'), and use the same form for every person (she went, not 'she wents').

examples.en: Yesterday I went to the market.
We had lunch at the kantin at twelve.
examples.id: Kami makan siang di kantin jam dua belas.

examples.en: My sister bought a new bag last week.
examples.id: Kakak perempuanku membeli tas baru minggu lalu.

id.title: Bentuk lampau tidak beraturan yang umum
id.explanation: Kebanyakan kata kerja ditambah -ed (walked), tapi banyak kata kerja yang sering dipakai punya bentuk lampau sendiri, tanpa aturan: go → went, have → had, get → got, see → saw, eat → ate, buy → bought, make → made, come → came, take → took, say → said. Hafalkan sebagai kosakata. Jangan tambah -ed (bukan 'goed'), dan bentuknya sama untuk semua orang (she went, bukan 'she wents').

keyPoints.title: Negatives and questions with did + base verb
keyPoints.explanation: Negative: didn't (did not) + base verb: I didn't go. Question: Did + subject + base verb: Did you see the film? Wh-question: What did you eat? did already shows the past, so the main verb goes back to its base form: not 'didn't went' or 'Did you saw'. Short answers: Yes, I did. / No, she didn't.

examples.en: I didn't go to school yesterday.
Did you see the film? — Yes, I did.
What did you eat for dinner?
examples.id: Kamu makan apa untuk makan malam?

id.title: Kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan dengan did + kata kerja dasar
id.explanation: Negatif: didn't (did not) + kata kerja dasar: I didn't go. Pertanyaan: Did + subjek + kata kerja dasar: Did you see the film? Pertanyaan dengan kata tanya: What did you eat? did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu, jadi kata kerja utamanya kembali ke bentuk dasar: bukan 'didn't went' atau 'Did you saw'. Jawaban singkat: Yes, I did. / No, she didn't.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the past of 'go': Rina ___ to Bandung last week.
guidedPractice.hint: go is irregular: it doesn't take -ed.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the past of 'have': We ___ lunch at the kantin at twelve yesterday.
Make it negative: I saw Pak Hasan at the office.
expected: i didn't see pak hasan at the office
i did not see pak hasan at the office
guidedPractice.hint: didn't + base verb: saw goes back to see.

guidedPractice.prompt: Make a question: She took an ojek to the station.
expected: did she take an ojek to the station
guidedPractice.hint: Did + she + base verb (take, not took).

independentPractice.prompt: Translate: Tadi pagi saya bangun jam enam.
expected: i got up at six this morning
this morning i got up at six
i got up at 6 this morning
this morning i got up at 6
i woke up at six this morning
this morning i woke up at six
i woke up at 6 this morning
this morning i woke up at 6
independentPractice.hint: bangun = get up, and get → got.

independentPractice.prompt: Translate: Mereka tidak datang ke pesta.
expected: they didn't come to the party
they did not come to the party

independentPractice.prompt: Answer with a short answer (no): Did you buy the tickets?

assessment.prompt: Complete with the past of 'buy': Last Saturday Sari ___ a new phone at the mall.
assessment.rubric: Correct: bought. 'buyed' = 40 (right idea, regular ending on an irregular verb). 'buys' / 'buy' = 20 (not past). 'brought' = 50 (a different verb, bring).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Last night we eated at a warung.
acceptableAnswers: last night we ate at a warung
we ate at a warung last night
assessment.rubric: Correct: Last night we ate at a warung. 'eat' = 30 (not past). 'eaten' = 40. 'at the warung' with 'ate' = 90. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Change to the past and start with 'Yesterday': I go to the office by bus.
acceptableAnswers: yesterday i went to the office by bus
assessment.rubric: Correct: Yesterday I went to the office by bus. 'Yesterday I go…' = 20 (the most common error: the verb must change). 'goed' = 40. 'Yesterday I was go…' = 30. Missing 'Yesterday' but 'went' correct = 80.

assessment.prompt: Make it negative: Budi went to work yesterday.
acceptableAnswers: budi didn't go to work yesterday
budi did not go to work yesterday
assessment.rubric: Correct: Budi didn't / did not go to work yesterday. 'didn't went' = 50 (did already shows the past). 'Budi not went' = 30. 'doesn't go' = 30. 'wasn't go' = 30.

assessment.prompt: Translate: Saya tidak sarapan tadi pagi.
acceptableAnswers: i didn't have breakfast this morning
i did not have breakfast this morning
this morning i didn't have breakfast
this morning i did not have breakfast
i didn't eat breakfast this morning
i did not eat breakfast this morning
this morning i didn't eat breakfast
this morning i did not eat breakfast
assessment.rubric: Correct: I didn't have breakfast this morning ('eat breakfast' also fine). 'didn't had' = 50. 'I don't have breakfast' = 30 (present). 'I not have breakfast' = 20. Missing 'this morning' = 70.

assessment.prompt: Make a question: You saw Rina at the market.
acceptableAnswers: did you see rina at the market
assessment.rubric: Correct: Did you see Rina at the market? 'Did you saw…' = 50 (did already shows the past). Statement order with a question mark = 20. 'Do you see…' = 30. 'Were you see…' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Write the question for this answer, starting with 'Where': I went to Bogor last weekend.
acceptableAnswers: where did you go last weekend
assessment.rubric: Correct: Where did you go last weekend? 'Where did you went' = 50. 'Where you went' = 30 (statement order, no did). 'Where do you go' = 30 (present). 'Where were you go' = 20. 'Where were you last weekend' = 60 (natural, but not with did).

material.title: Verbs with their own past form

blocks.text: In the last lesson you added **-ed** to show the past: *walk → walked, study → studied*. Verbs that follow this rule are **regular** (beraturan). But many of the most common verbs are **irregular** (tidak beraturan): they have their **own past form**, and there's no rule to work it out. You simply learn them, like new words. The good news: there aren't many you need every day, and the past form is the **same for every person**: *I went, she went, they went*.

id.text: Di pelajaran sebelumnya kamu menambah **-ed** untuk menunjukkan masa lalu: *walk → walked, study → studied*. Kata kerja yang mengikuti aturan ini disebut **regular** (beraturan). Tapi banyak kata kerja yang paling sering dipakai justru **irregular** (tidak beraturan): mereka punya **bentuk lampau sendiri**, dan tidak ada aturan untuk menebaknya. Kamu cukup menghafalnya, seperti kosakata baru. Kabar baiknya: yang dipakai sehari-hari tidak banyak, dan bentuk lampaunya **sama untuk semua orang**: *I went, she went, they went*.

id.note: Kami makan siang jam dua belas.

rows.note: I saw Budi at the bank.
I took a bus to work.

blocks.text: Two common mistakes: adding **-ed** anyway (*goed, eated, buyed, taked*) and adding **-s** for he/she (*she wents*). Irregular verbs never take -ed, and the past never takes -s: **She went home.** Learn the pairs together, out loud: *go–went, eat–ate, buy–bought*.

id.text: Dua kesalahan yang sering terjadi: tetap menambah **-ed** (*goed, eated, buyed, taked*) dan menambah **-s** untuk he/she (*she wents*). Kata kerja tidak beraturan tidak pernah ditambah -ed, dan bentuk lampau tidak pernah ditambah -s: **She went home.** Hafalkan pasangannya sekaligus sambil diucapkan: *go–went, eat–ate, buy–bought*.

blocks.prompt: Dewi ___ a cake for her mother's birthday.
blocks.explain: make is irregular: its past is made. 'maked' adds -ed to an irregular verb, and 'makes' is the present.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Dewi ___ a cake for her mother's birthday.
id.explain: make itu tidak beraturan: bentuk lampaunya made. 'maked' menambah -ed pada kata kerja tidak beraturan, dan 'makes' itu bentuk sekarang.

id.title: Kata kerja dengan bentuk lampau sendiri

blocks.text: In Indonesian the verb never changes: *Saya pergi ke pasar* (now) and *Kemarin saya pergi ke pasar* (past) use the same *pergi*. Only the time word (*kemarin, tadi pagi, minggu lalu*) shows the past. In English the **verb changes too**: *I go* → **I went**. So **Yesterday I go to the market** is wrong: say **Yesterday I went to the market.** Past time words you know: **yesterday, last night, last week, this morning** (when it's already afternoon), **two days ago**.

id.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kata kerja tidak pernah berubah: *Saya pergi ke pasar* (sekarang) dan *Kemarin saya pergi ke pasar* (masa lalu) memakai *pergi* yang sama. Hanya kata waktunya (*kemarin, tadi pagi, minggu lalu*) yang menunjukkan masa lalu. Dalam bahasa Inggris **kata kerjanya juga berubah**: *I go* → **I went**. Jadi **Yesterday I go to the market** itu salah: ucapkan **Yesterday I went to the market.** Kata waktu lampau yang sudah kamu kenal: **yesterday, last night, last week, this morning** (kalau sekarang sudah siang), **two days ago**.

rows.en: I got a message from my boss last night.
rows.id: Tadi malam saya dapat pesan dari bos saya.

rows.en: Pak Hasan came to the office at eight.
rows.id: Pak Hasan datang ke kantor jam delapan.

rows.en: We took a taxi to the airport two days ago.
rows.id: Dua hari yang lalu kami naik taksi ke bandara.

blocks.text: **get** has many meanings, and so does **got**: *I got a message* (dapat), *I got home at nine* (sampai di rumah), *I got up at five* (bangun). **take** is also used for transport: *I took a bus* = saya naik bus.

id.text: **get** punya banyak arti, begitu juga **got**: *I got a message* (dapat), *I got home at nine* (sampai di rumah), *I got up at five* (bangun). **take** juga dipakai untuk kendaraan: *I took a bus* = saya naik bus.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence means 'Kemarin saya melihat Budi di kantor'?
options: Yesterday I see Budi at the office.
Yesterday I saw Budi at the office.
Yesterday I seed Budi at the office.
blocks.explain: yesterday = past, so the verb changes: see → saw. 'see' keeps the present (the Indonesian habit), and 'seed' adds -ed to an irregular verb.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang artinya 'Kemarin saya melihat Budi di kantor'?
id.explain: yesterday = masa lalu, jadi kata kerjanya berubah: see → saw. 'see' tetap bentuk sekarang (kebiasaan dari bahasa Indonesia), dan 'seed' menambah -ed pada kata kerja tidak beraturan.

blocks.text: To say you didn't do something, use **didn't** (= did not) + the **base verb** (kata kerja dasar: the dictionary form, like *go, eat, see*): *I went* → **I didn't go**. Why not 'didn't went'? Because **did** is the past of *do*, so **did already shows the past**. The main verb doesn't need to show it again: it goes back to its base form. You know this from the present: *She works* → *She doesn't work* (does takes the -s, so work loses it). Same idea: **did takes the past**. It works for every person and for regular verbs too: *I didn't watch TV* (not 'didn't watched').

id.text: Untuk bilang kamu tidak melakukan sesuatu, pakai **didn't** (= did not) + **kata kerja dasar** (bentuk kamus, seperti *go, eat, see*): *I went* → **I didn't go**. Kenapa bukan 'didn't went'? Karena **did** adalah bentuk lampau dari *do*, jadi **did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu**. Kata kerja utamanya tidak perlu menunjukkannya lagi: ia kembali ke bentuk dasar. Kamu sudah tahu ini dari bentuk sekarang: *She works* → *She doesn't work* (does mengambil -s, jadi work kehilangan -s). Idenya sama: **did mengambil masa lalunya**. Berlaku untuk semua orang dan juga untuk kata kerja beraturan: *I didn't watch TV* (bukan 'didn't watched').

rows.en: I didn't go to the gym yesterday.
rows.id: Kemarin saya tidak pergi ke gym.

rows.en: Sari didn't eat meat at the party.
rows.id: Sari tidak makan daging di pesta itu.

rows.note: regular verbs too: watched → didn't watch

id.note: kata kerja beraturan juga: watched → didn't watch

blocks.text: The past shows **only once**: **didn't go**, not 'didn't went'. And don't just put *not* before the verb as in Indonesian *tidak pergi*: 'I not went' is wrong. With **was/were** there's no did: *I wasn't hungry* (not 'I didn't was hungry').

id.text: Masa lalu cukup ditunjukkan **satu kali**: **didn't go**, bukan 'didn't went'. Dan jangan hanya menaruh *not* sebelum kata kerja seperti *tidak pergi* dalam bahasa Indonesia: 'I not went' itu salah. Dengan **was/were** tidak pakai did: *I wasn't hungry* (bukan 'I didn't was hungry').

blocks.prompt: We ___ the bus this morning. We took an ojek.
blocks.explain: didn't + base verb: did already shows the past, so take stays take. 'not took' is missing did.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: We ___ the bus this morning. We took an ojek.
id.explain: didn't + kata kerja dasar: did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu, jadi take tetap take. 'not took' tidak memakai did.

id.title: Kalimat negatif: didn't + kata kerja dasar

blocks.text: For a yes/no question, put **Did** before the **subject** (who you ask about: *you, Rina, your parents*), then the **base verb**: *You went to Bali.* → **Did you go to Bali?** Again, did shows the past, so not 'Did you went'. Short answers use did: **Yes, I did.** / **No, I didn't.** For questions with a question word, put the word first: **What did you eat? Where did Rina stay? When did they come?** Indonesian asks with normal order (*Kamu pergi ke mana?*), but English needs **did** before the subject.

id.text: Untuk pertanyaan ya/tidak, taruh **Did** di depan **subjek** (siapa yang kamu tanyakan: *you, Rina, your parents*), lalu **kata kerja dasar**: *You went to Bali.* → **Did you go to Bali?** Sekali lagi, did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu, jadi bukan 'Did you went'. Jawaban singkat memakai did: **Yes, I did.** / **No, I didn't.** Untuk pertanyaan dengan kata tanya, taruh kata tanyanya di depan: **What did you eat? Where did Rina stay? When did they come?** Bahasa Indonesia bertanya dengan urutan biasa (*Kamu pergi ke mana?*), tapi bahasa Inggris perlu **did** sebelum subjek.

rows.en: Did Rina come to the meeting? — No, she didn't.
Did they have a good holiday? — Yes, they did.
What did you buy at the mall?

rows.note: did = helper, do = the real verb (melakukan)

id.note: did = kata bantu, do = kata kerja sebenarnya (melakukan)

blocks.text: Don't mix **was/were** with **did**: *Were you go to Bali?* is wrong. Use **Did** with other verbs (*Did you go…?*) and **Was/Were** only with no other verb (*Were you in Bali?*). And don't just add a question mark to a normal sentence: **Did you see the match?**, not 'You saw the match?'.

id.text: Jangan mencampur **was/were** dengan **did**: *Were you go to Bali?* itu salah. Pakai **Did** dengan kata kerja lain (*Did you go…?*) dan **Was/Were** hanya kalau tidak ada kata kerja lain (*Were you in Bali?*). Dan jangan hanya menambah tanda tanya pada kalimat biasa: **Did you see the match?**, bukan 'You saw the match?'.

blocks.prompt: ___ you eat at the warung yesterday?
blocks.explain: eat is a verb, and yesterday is the past → Did. 'Were' is for sentences with no other verb, and 'Do' is the present.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ you eat at the warung yesterday?
id.explain: eat itu kata kerja, dan yesterday itu masa lalu → Did. 'Were' untuk kalimat tanpa kata kerja lain, dan 'Do' itu bentuk sekarang.

blocks.text: Monday morning at the office: *What did you do at the weekend? — I went to Bogor with my family. We ate sate and took a lot of photos.* (*at the weekend* is British; Americans say *on the weekend*.) At home: *Did you buy rice? — No, sorry, I didn't. I forgot.* (*forget → forgot*, another irregular verb.) After a trip: *We had a great time, but we didn't see the sunrise.*

id.text: Senin pagi di kantor: *What did you do at the weekend? — I went to Bogor with my family. We ate sate and took a lot of photos.* (*at the weekend* itu bahasa Inggris British; orang Amerika bilang *on the weekend*.) Di rumah: *Did you buy rice? — No, sorry, I didn't. I forgot.* (*forget → forgot*, kata kerja tidak beraturan lainnya.) Setelah jalan-jalan: *We had a great time, but we didn't see the sunrise.*

suggestedQuestions: Why do I say 'didn't go' and not 'didn't went'?
How do I answer 'What did you do at the weekend?'
Is there a trick to remember irregular verbs?

flashcards.back: What did you eat last night?

id.intro: Hai! Kamu sudah bisa bercerita dengan kata kerja -ed: I walked, I watched. Tapi kata kerja yang paling sering dipakai punya bentuk lampau sendiri: go → went, eat → ate, buy → bought. Di pelajaran ini kamu belajar sepuluh yang paling penting, juga cara bilang apa yang tidak kamu lakukan dan bertanya Did you…? Pemanasan: kemarin kamu makan apa? Coba jawab 'I ate …'.
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana menjawab 'What did you do at the weekend?'
Ada trik untuk menghafal kata kerja tidak beraturan?

assessment.psi-1: Lengkapi dengan bentuk lampau dari 'buy': Last Saturday Sari ___ a new phone at the mall.
assessment.psi-2: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Last night we eated at a warung.
assessment.psi-3: Ubah ke bentuk lampau dan mulai dengan 'Yesterday': I go to the office by bus.
assessment.psi-4: Ubah ke kalimat negatif: Budi went to work yesterday.
assessment.psi-5: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Inggris: Saya tidak sarapan tadi pagi.
assessment.psi-6: Ubah ke kalimat tanya: You saw Rina at the market.
